items.stem: Why does AI change the phishing threat landscape for defenders?

options.text: Attackers can generate more convincing, tailored lures at scale
options.rationale: Correct: generative AI lowers the cost of high-quality, targeted phishing.

options.text: Phishing is no longer possible with AI around
options.rationale: AI does not eliminate phishing; it can amplify it.

options.text: AI makes all emails automatically safe
options.rationale: AI does not make emails safe.

items.explanation: Correct: generative AI lowers the cost of high-quality, targeted phishing.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep AI-assisted security operations safe? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Require human approval before high-impact automated response actions
options.rationale: Correct: human approval prevents damaging automated mistakes.

options.text: Verify AI alert rankings before acting on them
options.rationale: Correct: verification guards against false confidence.

options.text: Auto-block based on raw AI output with no review
options.rationale: Unreviewed automated blocking can cause outages or miss threats.

options.text: Feed sensitive logs into any public AI tool
options.rationale: Sending sensitive logs to uncontrolled tools risks leakage.

items.explanation: Correct: human approval prevents damaging automated mistakes.

items.stem: An AI tool ranks an alert as low priority. What is the appropriate analyst response?

options.text: Treat the ranking as a hint and verify before dismissing a potential threat
options.rationale: Correct: AI rankings can be wrong, so verification protects against missed incidents.

options.text: Dismiss the alert immediately without checking
options.rationale: Blindly trusting the ranking can let real threats through.

options.text: Assume the AI considered every context perfectly

options.rationale: Ignoring the triage signal entirely wastes capacity; verify instead.

items.explanation: Correct: AI rankings can be wrong, so verification protects against missed incidents.
